Holds typically last 2–7 business days, depending on the reason [1]. You'll be notified of the hold on your deposit receipt (at an ATM or financial center), on your mobile deposit confirmation screen, or by email or mail if one is placed later [3].

If you'd prefer to avoid holds altogether, consider asking those paying you to use electronic methods like direct deposit, ACH transfers, or Zelle® instead [7].

When you deposit a check through mobile banking, funds are generally available the next business day [3].

Here's how it works:

- If you deposit before the cutoff time on a business day, the deposit processes that night and is usually available the next business day [3].
- Cutoff times depend on your time zone. Eastern or Central time zone accounts have a 9:00 p.m. ET cutoff; Mountain or Pacific time zones have an 8:00 p.m. cutoff [1].
- If you deposit after cutoff or on a weekend/holiday, it's processed the next business day and generally available the business day after that [3].

A hold may delay availability in some cases [3]. Bank of America considers deposit type, amount, and your customer relationship when deciding funds availability [7].
